correctness.rationale: For fixed radius, adjacent full-window means differ by a translated endpoint difference with at most one negative-to-positive sign change for valley data. Every clipped ball at an interior vertex is reproducible from a more exterior comparison vertex; every nonclipped ball is bounded by full-window valley comparisons, with the boundary-window values also reproducible from exterior vertices. This proves quasiconvexity/valley shape of the entire centered maximal function. Prefix and suffix means have their maxima at an endpoint of their radius lists, hence Mf(0)=max(f(0),mu) and Mf(n-1)=max(f(n-1),mu). Since Mf>=mu and Var(f)=A+B, the displayed exact positive-part and quantitative deficit inequalities follow by algebra. Any equality with nonzero variation forces one endpoint excess to vanish and all interior values to equal the minimum; conversely endpoint spikes attain the coefficient. Symmetric two-endpoint spikes attain the mass-gap bound. The standalone exact-rational script completed 13652 valley profiles of lengths 3..10 and four additional rational profiles; this finite check is corroboration, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 arXiv article formulates the unrestricted finite-path variation constant as Conjecture 5, proves P4 and computationally treats small graphs, and does not prove a uniform all-length valley subclass. An accessible published monotone-data statement and an already available peak-shaped theorem do not imply the genuinely two-endpoint-high valley case; the input f=(1,0,...,0,1) is neither globally monotone nor single-peaked. The 2021/2025 Bilz–Weigt setting is on the infinite lattice with indicators or an attachment hypothesis, whereas the 2019 Ramos valley lemma concerns output on detachment intervals; neither states this finite-path coefficient and sharp endpoint-mass gap. Comparison of claim implications and the performed searches supports originality to best current knowledge, with historic coverage risk expressly retained.

value.rationale: The source conjectures a sharp finite-path variation coefficient at all sizes. The nonnegative single-trough class is a natural genuinely nonmonotone family not covered by the established monotone and single-peak subclasses. The new proof identifies a structural preservation property of the centered graph maximal operator despite boundary truncation and supplies the exact sharp contraction coefficient and equality cases at every order. The endpoint-mass defect is strictly positive whenever both path endpoints rise above the trough and is itself sharp for symmetric endpoint masses. This materially constrains potential counterexample geometry: no profile with only one trough can be a counterexample to the unrestricted conjecture. It does not claim resolution of that conjecture.
